context: a single passage from a letter by John Higgins, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: Your Tenant at Beesby (Mr Hardy) has spent large sums of money in underdraining his Farm with Tiles, and otherwise has managed it exceedingly well; he found his Fold Yard, and Cattle Sheds too small for the proper treading down of the Straw, and as I (on your behalf) refused to build more; Mr. Hardy three years ago spent £105 in constructing an additional yard, and Cattle accommodation of best bricks and foreign Timber adjoining to his other yard, which work is done in a very substantial and permanent manner.
I am very glad to hear of the increased Rent, which will make my Farm a very good investment; & I truly thank you for your kind attention to my interests.
